title: Robotic adhesive dispensing
summary: A low-cost robotic end-effector that brought repeatability and faster cycle times to wall fabrication.
description: A low-cost robotic end-effector that brought repeatability and faster cycle times to wall fabrication.
objectives: Reduce the manual adhesive application bottleneck in a wall fabrication pilot.
Improve bead consistency with a robust, low-cost dispensing solution.
contributions: Evaluated actuator concepts and selected an off-the-shelf electric caulking gun.
Designed the quick-change mount, pneumatic trigger actuation, and tube support.
Programmed robot paths and process logic in RAPID using RobotStudio and the IRC5 controller.

process.title: Adapt proven hardware
process.body: An off-the-shelf caulking gun reduced cost and deployment time. A printed mount interfaces with the robot’s tool-change system.

process.title: Design around failure modes
process.body: A U-bolt supports the tube to reduce stress on the tool’s plastic joints. A limit switch detects an empty tube and initiates a production interruption and reload sequence.

process.title: Tune the full process
process.body: Varied robot speed, gun settings, and tip distance, then refined lift-off and stud-to-plate sequencing.

results: Reduced adhesive application time by 54.5% compared with a professional human framer, as documented in the supplied project description.
Implemented the tested end-effector in pilot production with a consistent bead.
